title: One-day courses at a country park

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Part 1. You will hear a man phoning a country park to ask about some one-day courses. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 5.

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: Good morning, Greenhill Country Park, Karen speaking. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Hi. I picked up a leaflet about your one-day courses at the visitor centre last month, but I can't find it anywhere now. I was hoping you could tell me about them again.

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: Of course. Was there a particular course you were interested in?

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Well, a few, actually. The first one was birdwatching for beginners. I think that was in early April. The 5th, was it?

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: That was last year's date. This year it's a week later, on the 12th of April. It's eighteen pounds, and we lend everyone a pair of binoculars for the day, so you don't need your own.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Oh, great. Could I book a place?

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: I'm sorry, it's fully booked at the moment. I can put your name on the waiting list, though. People do sometimes cancel.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: No, don't worry. What about the nature photography course? That's in May, isn't it?

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: Yes, Saturday the 3rd of May. It's forty-five pounds. It used to be fifty, but we've brought the price down this year because we don't provide lunch any more.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: And what kind of things do people take photos of?

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: Birds move too fast for beginners, so the tutor concentrates on wild flowers, insects and trees. He says trees are the best subject for learning about light.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Sounds good. Do I need a proper camera?

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: No, the camera on your phone is fine. Most people use their phones these days, and the tutor shows you some useful settings.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: OK. Now, I'm quite keen on the map reading course as well. I get lost very easily.

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: That one's on the 26th of April, and it costs thirty pounds. It's run by Peter Hollis. A lot of people assume he was in the army, but in fact he worked here as a ranger for over twenty years, so he knows every path in the park.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Will I need any equipment?

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: We provide the maps and the compasses. All you need to bring is a pencil, because you mark your route on the map as you go.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 6 to 10.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: And there was a course on finding wild food, wasn't there?

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: Yes, wild food foraging. It was planned for the 10th of May, but the tutor's away that weekend, so it's been moved to the 17th of May. It's thirty-eight pounds.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: What do you actually do on the day?

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: You spend the morning collecting things like wild garlic, nettles and mushrooms. Then everything you find is cooked for lunch on a camp stove. People say that's the best part of the day.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: That sounds like fun. I also saw something about dry-stone walling.

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: That's on the 7th of June. You learn to build walls from stones without any cement. It's a skilled job and the group is very small, so it's a bit more expensive. It's eighty-four pounds.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Eighty-four. Hmm.

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: It's still good value. A similar course at the agricultural college costs over a hundred.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: I suppose so. Do I need to bring anything?

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: We provide gloves and all the tools. But the stones are very heavy, so you must wear strong boots. Trainers aren't allowed, I'm afraid.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Fair enough. And the last one I remember was for families. Bushcraft?

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: Yes, bushcraft for families, on the 21st of June. It's twenty-five pounds per person. The children learn how to build a shelter from branches.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Do they light fires too? My kids would love that.

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: We used to do that, but we stopped for safety reasons. Instead, there's a session on recognising animal tracks. The children look for footprints in the mud and work out which animal made them.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: They'd enjoy that. Right, I think I'd like to book the map reading course for myself, and the bushcraft day for all of us. There are four of us, two adults and two children.

lines.speaker: KAREN
lines.text: Lovely. Let me just get the booking form up on my screen.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: That is the end of Part 1.

groups.instructions: Complete the table below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

Everything that is collected is cooked for {7}.

evidence.quote: This year it's a week later, on the 12th of April.

pairs: This year it's … on the 12th of April
1.why: The man guesses the 5th of April, but Karen corrects him: this year the course is a week later, on the 12th of April.
1.trap: The 5th was last year's date. When a speaker corrects the other person, the corrected information is the answer.

evidence.quote: It's forty-five pounds. It used to be fifty

2.why: The photography course costs £45 now. The pound sign is already in the table, so write just the number.
2.trap: Fifty pounds was the old price. 'Used to be' tells you it is no longer true.

evidence.quote: the tutor concentrates on wild flowers, insects and trees

3.why: Wild flowers and insects are already in the note, so the missing third thing is trees. Keep the plural form you hear.
3.trap: Birds are mentioned first, but Karen says they move too fast for beginners, so they are not part of the course.

evidence.quote: he worked here as a ranger for over twenty years

pairs: worked as a … for over 20 years
worked here as a … for over twenty years
4.why: Peter Hollis worked at the park as a ranger for more than twenty years.
4.trap: People think he was in the army, but 'in fact' shows that this idea is wrong.

evidence.quote: All you need to bring is a pencil

pairs: All you need to bring is a
5.why: The only thing learners must bring is a pencil, to mark their route on the map.
5.trap: Maps and compasses are mentioned, but the park provides them, so you do not bring them.

evidence.quote: so it's been moved to the 17th of May

pairs: it's been moved to the 17th of May
6.why: The foraging course was planned for the 10th of May, but it has moved to the 17th of May.
6.trap: The 10th of May was the first plan. Words like 'was planned' and 'moved to' signal a change of date.

evidence.quote: everything you find is cooked for lunch on a camp stove

7.why: The food people collect in the morning is cooked for lunch.
7.trap: 'Morning' is when people collect the food, not what the food is cooked for.

8.why: Karen gives the price as £84, and the man repeats it. Write just the number, because the pound sign is in the table.
8.trap: 'Over a hundred' is the price of a similar course at a different place, the agricultural college.

9.why: The stones are heavy, so learners must wear strong boots.
9.trap: Gloves are mentioned first, but the park provides them. Trainers are not allowed.

evidence.quote: there's a session on recognising animal tracks

10.why: Children learn to recognise animal tracks, which Karen explains are footprints in the mud. Either word fits the gap.
10.trap: Lighting fires is not on the course any more. Karen says they stopped it for safety reasons.
